issue_context.title: Json source generator compiler error using reserved property names and DefaultIgnoreCondition
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-json, @gregsdennis See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Json-source-generator-compiler-error-usi/10535386)._ --- [severity:I'm unable to use this version] In .net8 using JSON source generator with property names that are preserved c# names and using JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull, invalid sources will be generated. [SourceGenBug.zip](https://aka.ms/dc/file?name=Bf7a5de6e950a4d23bd03eb3e0d802f5a638374833787755809_SourceGenBug.zip&tid=f7a5de6e950a4d23bd03eb3e0d802f5a638374833787755809) ``` public class Model { public string type { get; set; } public string alias { get; set; } } [JsonSourceGenerationOptions(DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)] [JsonSerializable(typeof(Model))] internal partial class ModelContext : JsonSerializerContext { } ``` This will generate source with a lot of compilation errors. It wil generate ``` string __value_@type = ((global::Model)value).@type; if (__value_@type != null) { writer.WriteString(PropName_type, __value_@type); } ``` In dotnet 7 it would generate: ``` if (value.@type != null) { writer.WriteString(PropName_type, value.@type); } ``` --- ### Original Comments #### Feedback Bot on 12/6/2023, 06:10 PM: (private comment, text removed) --- ### Original Solutions (no solutions)
Author: vsfeedback
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Text.Json`
Milestone: -
Appears to be a regression caused by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/87725, we should service .NET 8.

review_comments: If we were prefixing it the variable name with `__value_`, in the case of `@` should suffix it with `__value_` instead of trimming? I mean we will have something like `@type__value_`.
We could. I figured we shouldn't change the naming convention for the servicing fix.
I was just thinking in possible variable names conflict . I imaging if you have a case like two names `something` and `@something`. Is it a possible case?

`something` and `@something` are equivalent identifiers, e.g.

https://sharplab.io/#v2:CYLg1APgAgTAjAWAFBQMwAJboMIG9nqGYYCWAdgC7oCyAFAJTr5JGvrlUUCmAzlQLzoALDADcBNoSgB2TFG590YdHHEsiAX2QagA

I don't believe it is possible for conflicts to exist in code that compiles.
